contract.review_scope: Full retained body, necessary private dynamic/literal interpretation, direct source behavior and explicit operational gaps.
contract.purpose: Build a selected configuration-count summary from a JSON selection document. The retained body constructs dynamic UNION SELECT statements over a fixed set of configuration tables; it does not load or change those configuration rows.
inputs_defaults: Only explicit declaration defaults permit omission; catalog has_default_value is not used to infer T-SQL defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: There is no ISJSON check or TRY/CATCH. Invalid JSON, incompatible nested JSON values, conversion/collation or query-construction failures propagate. QUOTENAME handles quoting of each input element but is not an arbitrary-length serializer: unsupported/oversized values can produce NULL; STRING_AGG skips NULL inputs, and a NULL aggregate leads to a skipped branch. No input length/type validation establishes a complete selection round-trip. FormattedKey has no unique key. Duplicate JSON keys can aggregate values, and the UNION ALL empty-array row can coexist with another row for the same key; SELECT assignment of @values has no ordering guarantee. COUNT(description) and COUNT(object_id) omit NULL detail values, while COUNT(*) counts rows. COUNT(DISTINCT rating_id) omits NULL identifiers. These are source-specific counts, not interchangeable measures of configured entities. No caller permissions, effective warehouse/company configuration, deployment status or runtime result counts are established by these summaries.
output_shape: When at least one branch contributes query text, one dynamic result set has RecordType, NumberOfRecords, Description and ConfigType. UNION removes duplicate whole result rows; there is no final ORDER BY. A selection that contributes no query executes no sp_executesql and produces no summary result set; this is distinct from an executed aggregate returning a zero count. Most branches return a fixed label plus COUNT(*); header/detail branches group by selected record type. CARRIER_EDI_REFERENCE instead counts distinct rating_id for rows with customer IS NULL.

effects.binding_limit: No captured local application object identity is asserted. This is a system/cross-database reference, a dynamic-operation marker, or an unresolved local name; the exact kind is specified separately.

ordered_branches.explanation: Trim @configsToLoad, parse top-level properties with OPENJSON and CROSS APPLY OPENJSON to their values, aggregate single-quote QUOTENAME values into a parenthesized comma-separated list, and store key/value strings in #configsKeyValData. Empty-array properties receive a separate empty-string row. The generic, system and filter header/detail branches inject these quoted value lists into fixed RECORD_TYPE IN predicates. Generic and filter summaries count non-null detail columns through LEFT JOIN and group by the header record type. The system-config branch adds a fixed exclusion combining a small SYS_KEY list and RECORD_TYPE. Because the extra predicate references the nullable detail side, a header with no matching detail is filtered by three-valued logic rather than reliably returned as a zero-count header. Other branches are selected by property existence plus nonempty serialized value checks; some additionally use LIKE against the serialized value. They then append fixed aggregate SELECT templates, often counting an entire table rather than applying each selected element as a row predicate. The generated query begins with a leading UNION token; a final prefix check removes six characters before sp_executesql. The temporary table is dropped at the normal tail. There is no local error cleanup path. Creates, inserts into and drops local #configsKeyValData. No persistent DML appears in the retained body or reviewed dynamic SELECT templates. sp_executesql @query without a separate parameter definition/value list; constructed input is used in fixed IN-list branches. No other procedure call is present.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
